body.statement: Can \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{out}}\) be constructed so that, for rational empirical cell frequencies and rational \(\eta\), it returns exactly \(\mathcal D_n\), emits a valid inclusion or exclusion certificate for every labeled DAG, terminates with delay polynomial in the input bit length and \(d\) between successive output source-forest classes, and preserves the coverage conclusion of \(\text{thm:outer-fiber-confidence}\)?
body.justification: The population geometry suggests an exact output-sensitive alternative to generic semialgebraic elimination, but its complexity is genuinely open.
body.gap: Existing causal-model inversion papers do not exploit a source-forest quotient, and the PB-SCM papers provide point algorithms rather than certified outward enumeration.
body.consumer: A positive answer would make honest full-fiber confidence reporting computationally usable beyond very small event systems.

obligation.what_is_open: Constructing an exact enumerator for \(\mathcal D_n\) with delay polynomial in the input bit length and \(d\), together with polynomially checkable inclusion or exclusion certificates for every labeled DAG.
obligation.obstruction: The source-forest theorem is pointwise in a realizable coefficient vector, whereas \(C_n\) ranges over vectors whose skeleton and head signatures can change. Exact membership of one graph is an existential nonlinear feasibility problem with strict parameter inequalities and with \(\epsilon_n=\sqrt{\log(2|I_4|/\eta)/(2n)}\). The frozen core supplies neither a polynomial-time feasibility oracle nor a complexity lower bound, so a polynomial-delay conclusion cannot be derived honestly.
obligation.attempted: Reduce membership graph by graph using the reverse-topological decoder, interval screening, and source-forest enumeration. The decoder is decisive at a fixed realizable vector, but interval screening is not complete when coefficient signs can cross zero inside \(C_n\), and exhaustive graph enumeration has no polynomial-delay guarantee. Generic quantifier elimination, even after denominator clearing, also supplies no such delay bound.
obligation.partial_result: For each fixed labeled DAG \(G\), membership \(G\in\mathcal D_n\) reduces to one finite existential feasibility problem over \(q\), \(\mu\), and \(\alpha\): impose \(q\in Q_n\), \(\mu_i>0\), \(0<\alpha_e<1\), and \(t_4(P_{G,\mu,\alpha})=T(q)\).  The root-cluster recursion makes the left side polynomial in \((\mu,\alpha)\), and multiplication by the positive powers of \(q_0\) appearing in \(T\) clears every rational denominator.  Thus an exact feasibility oracle followed by finite enumeration of labeled DAGs returns exactly \(\mathcal D_n\), and because it returns the set in the frozen definition, the coverage theorem remains valid.  This reduction supplies neither polynomial delay nor a polynomial-size inclusion or exclusion certificate.
